descripcion_es: Plans already decided and predictions based on what you can see.
resumen: Be going to + infinitive expresses intentions or plans decided before speaking and predictions based on present evidence. It is equivalent to Spanish “ir a + infinitivo”.

filas: subject + am / is / are + going to + infinitive
subject + am not / isn't / aren't + going to + infinitive
Am / Is / Are + subject + going to + infinitive?
Are you going to buy it?

items: An intention or plan already decided: I'm going to learn German next year.
A prediction with evidence you can see now: Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.
It is not used for decisions made at the moment of speaking: use will for that.

explicacion.texto: The verb be agrees with the subject (I am, he is, they are) and is never left out: “I going to” is wrong. After going to there is always the infinitive with no extra to.
With the verb go you can say I'm going to go to the gym, although in spoken English people often simply say I'm going to the gym (present continuous).
En inglés oral informal going to se pronuncia a menudo gonna; no conviene escribirlo en textos formales.

ejemplos.frase: I'm going to paint the kitchen this weekend.
ejemplos.traduccion: Voy a pintar la cocina este fin de semana.

ejemplos.frase: Be careful! You're going to fall.
Are they going to sell the house?
She isn't going to accept the offer.
ejemplos.traduccion: No va a aceptar la oferta.

ejemplos.frase: The team is losing 3-0. They're going to lose the match.
ejemplos.traduccion: El equipo pierde 3-0. Van a perder el partido.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I going to visit my aunt.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I'm going to visit my aunt.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: We are going to to travel.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Only one to: going to + infinitive.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Are you going to visiting Rome?
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Are you going to visit Rome?
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: After going to comes the infinitive, not -ing.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of be going to.
ejercicios.frase: My parents ___ (move) to the coast next year.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule on the card applies: the verb be agrees with the subject and is never left out. The clue is the subject My parents, which is equivalent to they and needs are. Then comes going to + infinitive without to: move. The result is are going to move (or 're going to move), a plan decided for next year.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Plural subject: are going to + infinitive.
ejercicios.traduccion: Mis padres se van a mudar a la costa el año que viene.

errores_previstos.respuesta: going to move
errores_previstos.explicacion: The verb be is missing, a typical mistake on the card: are going to move.

errores_previstos.respuesta: is going to move
errores_previstos.explicacion: My parents is plural: are, not is.

errores_previstos.respuesta: are going to moving
errores_previstos.explicacion: After going to comes the infinitive, not -ing.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of be going to.
ejercicios.frase: I ___ (start) a new diet on Monday.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule of agreement between be and the subject applies: with I you use am. The clues are the subject I and on Monday, a plan already decided. The form is am going to start, or the contraction 'm going to start, very common in spoken English.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Plan decided with I: am going to.
ejercicios.traduccion: Voy a empezar una dieta nueva el lunes.

errores_previstos.respuesta: going to start
errores_previstos.explicacion: The verb be is missing: I am going to start.

errores_previstos.respuesta: is going to start
errores_previstos.explicacion: With I the verb be is am.

errores_previstos.respuesta: am going to to start
errores_previstos.explicacion: There is one to too many: going to + infinitive without to.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the negative form of be going to.
ejercicios.explicacion: The negative form of be going to applies: the negation goes after be (is not or isn't), and going to + infinitive does not change. The clues are the subject He, third person singular, and the prompt not. isn't going to come, is not going to come and 's not going to come are all accepted, as they are three ways of writing the same thing.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Negative in the third person: isn't going to.
ejercicios.traduccion: Él no va a venir a la reunión.

errores_previstos.respuesta: doesn't going to come
errores_previstos.explicacion: Be going to does not form the negative with do; the negation goes with be: isn't going to.

errores_previstos.respuesta: not going to come
errores_previstos.explicacion: The verb be is missing: isn't going to come.

errores_previstos.respuesta: isn't going to coming
errores_previstos.explicacion: After going to comes the infinitive: come.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of be going to.
ejercicios.explicacion: The use of be going to for predictions based on present evidence, as shown on the card, applies. The clue is Look at that car!: the speaker can see something at that moment that anticipates the crash. The subject It (the car) needs is: is going to crash, or with the contraction 's going to crash.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Prediction based on what you can see.

errores_previstos.respuesta: will crash
errores_previstos.explicacion: Will expresses a prediction based on opinion; with visible evidence in front of you, use going to.

errores_previstos.respuesta: going to crash
errores_previstos.explicacion: The verb be is missing: is going to crash.

errores_previstos.respuesta: is going to crashing
errores_previstos.explicacion: After going to comes the infinitive, not -ing.

ejercicios.explicacion: The rule for questions with be going to applies: be and the subject are inverted, without do. The clue is the question word What at the beginning. The order is What + are + you + going to + do. As be is an auxiliary, do is not needed.
ejercicios.traduccion: ¿Qué vas a hacer después de la universidad?

por_opcion.are you going to: Correct: in the question be goes before the subject.
por_opcion.you are going to: Incorrect: it keeps the order of the affirmative; in a question with What you have to invert.
por_opcion.do you going to: Incorrect: be going to does not form questions with do; be is inverted.

ejercicios.frase: She has bought paint because she ___ her bedroom.
ejercicios.explicacion: The use of be going to for intentions decided before speaking applies. The clue is She has bought paint: the purchase shows that the decision has already been made. That is why the form is is going to paint, with is because the subject is she.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Plan already decided (she has bought the paint): going to.
ejercicios.traduccion: Ha comprado pintura porque va a pintar su dormitorio.

por_opcion.is going to paint: Correct: a plan already decided, shown by the purchase of the paint.
por_opcion.will paint: Incorrect: will expresses a decision made at the moment; here the decision was made earlier.
por_opcion.paints: Incorrect: the present simple would express a habit or a timetable, not a plan.

ejercicios.frase: The sky is black. It ___ rain.
ejercicios.explicacion: Two rules from the card apply: be going to for predictions based on present evidence, and be is compulsory. The clue is The sky is black, visible evidence of rain. The form is is going to: is agrees with it and cannot be left out.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Prediction with present evidence; be is compulsory.
ejercicios.traduccion: El cielo está negro. Va a llover.

por_opcion.is going to: Correct: a prediction with present evidence, with be included.
por_opcion.goes to: Incorrect: goes to means “moves towards (a place)”; it does not form the future.
por_opcion.going to: Incorrect: the verb be (is) is missing, and it is never left out.

ejercicios.enunciado: Turn the sentence into a question.
ejercicios.frase: They are going to get married.
respuestas: Are they going to get married?
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule for questions with be going to applies: be and the subject are inverted. The clue is the instruction to turn a sentence with They are going to into a question. Move are in front of they and leave going to get married unchanged, with a question mark at the end.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Be and the subject are inverted.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Do they going to get married?
errores_previstos.explicacion: Be going to does not form questions with do; are is inverted.

errores_previstos.respuesta: They are going to get married?
errores_previstos.explicacion: It only adds the question mark; in written English you must invert be and the subject.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Are they going to getting married?
errores_previstos.explicacion: After going to comes the infinitive get.

ejercicios.enunciado: Make the sentence negative (use the contraction isn't).
ejercicios.frase: Laura is going to study law.
respuestas: Laura isn't going to study law.
ejercicios.explicacion: The negative of be going to applies: the negation goes with be, and with Laura (third person) it is isn't. The clue is the instruction to use the contraction isn't. The rest does not change: going to study law. Doesn't is not used, because be already works as an auxiliary.
ejercicios.traduccion: Laura no va a estudiar Derecho.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Laura doesn't going to study law.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Be going to does not form the negative with do; be is made negative: isn't.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Laura isn't going to studying law.
errores_previstos.explicacion: After going to comes the infinitive study.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Laura is going to not study law.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The negation goes with be, not before the infinitive; besides, the exercise asks for isn't.

ejercicios.frase: We going to have a party on Friday.
respuestas: We are going to have a party on Friday.
We're going to have a party on Friday.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule on the card applies: the verb be agrees with the subject and is never left out. The clue is the subject We with no verb be before going to. The correction is We are going to (or We're going to), a plan decided for Friday.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The verb be is missing: are going to.
ejercicios.traduccion: Vamos a hacer una fiesta el viernes.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We going to have a party on Friday.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It leaves the sentence uncorrected: the verb be is missing.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We is going to have a party on Friday.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It adds be but without agreement: with we it is are.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We are go to have a party on Friday.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The structure is going to, not go to.

ejercicios.frase: Is your brother going to buying a car?
respuestas: Is your brother going to buy a car?
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule on the card applies: after going to there is always the infinitive without to, never the -ing form. The clue is buying after going to. The to in going to is the infinitive marker, not a preposition, so it requires the base form: buy.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: After going to comes the infinitive.
ejercicios.traduccion: ¿Tu hermano va a comprarse un coche?

errores_previstos.respuesta: Is your brother going to buying a car?
errores_previstos.explicacion: It leaves the sentence uncorrected: after going to comes the infinitive.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Is your brother going to bought a car?
errores_previstos.explicacion: After going to comes the infinitive, not the past.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Does your brother going to buy a car?
errores_previstos.explicacion: The question is formed with be, not with do.

ejercicios.frase: I'm going to to call the doctor.
respuestas: I'm going to call the doctor.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule on the card applies: going to + infinitive has only one to. The clue is the repeated to. The first to is part of going to and already acts as the infinitive marker, so the verb comes straight after it: I'm going to call the doctor.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: There is one to too many.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I'm going to to call the doctor.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It leaves the sentence uncorrected: there is one to too many.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I'm going call the doctor.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It removes the wrong to: you need exactly one, going to call.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I going to call the doctor.
errores_previstos.explicacion: As well as removing the to, it removes the verb be, which is compulsory.

respuestas: We are going to rent a flat
Are we going to rent a flat
ejercicios.explicacion: The basic order on the card applies: subject + be + going to + infinitive + complement. The clue is that there is a subject (we), be (are), going, to, the infinitive rent and the complement a flat. The question, with are before the subject, is also accepted, because when ordering without punctuation the same words allow both readings.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Subject + are going to + infinitive + complement.
ejercicios.traduccion: Vamos a alquilar un piso. (o, como pregunta: ¿Vamos a alquilar un piso?)

errores_previstos.respuesta: We are going to a flat rent
errores_previstos.explicacion: The infinitive goes immediately after going to, and the complement after it: rent a flat.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We going are to rent a flat
errores_previstos.explicacion: It breaks the structure: be goes before going to (are going to).

ejercicios.enunciado: Put the words in order to make a question.
respuestas: When is she going to leave
ejercicios.explicacion: The order of questions with be going to applies: question word + be + subject + going to + infinitive. The clues are the instruction to make a question and the presence of when. The result is When is she going to leave, with is before she.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Question word + is + subject + going to + infinitive.

errores_previstos.respuesta: When she is going to leave
errores_previstos.explicacion: It keeps the order of the affirmative; in a question be goes before the subject.

errores_previstos.respuesta: When is going she to leave
errores_previstos.explicacion: It puts the subject in the wrong place: when is she going to leave.

descripcion_larga_es: Be going to + infinitive is the simplest way to talk about plans and intentions already decided and about predictions based on what you can see. It is almost exactly equivalent to Spanish “ir a + infinitivo”, which helps a lot. Typical mistakes for Spanish speakers are forgetting the verb be (I going to), doubling to or putting -ing after going to.

contexto.que_es: It is a future form made up of the conjugated verb be (am, is, are), going to and the infinitive without to: I am going to travel. It expresses intentions decided before speaking and predictions supported by present evidence.
contexto.por_que_importa: It is one of the most frequent future forms in everyday conversation, especially for talking about plans. Using it well lets you distinguish what has already been decided from what is decided at the moment (will). Mistakes like I going to or going to visiting are very noticeable and lose marks even at basic levels.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: It is used when talking about plans (next year, on Monday, after university) and when predicting something from what you can see (Look!, The sky is black). A frequent signal is a previous action that shows the intention: she has bought paint, he has booked. Spanish speakers, guided by Spanish “voy a”, often forget am/is/are or add a second to.
